content:
rachel: quick follow-up on escrowed provisional capacity idea i floated — goal: let tenants buy short-lived guaranteed capacity slices that proxies honor without central round-trip, but still enforce fairness and abuse checks. sketch below.

emily: interested. main ops worry: how do we prevent escrowed tenants from gaming it (spinning up many sub-tenants or reusing tokens)?

rachel: plan: escrow token = signed voucher from controller containing tenant_id, capacity_tokens, window_ms, nonce, and a short TTL (<=10s). proxies validate signature and enforce local reserve. token consumption emits signed receipts back to the controller for billing/fraud reconciliation.

vik: receipts sound heavy. can receipts be sampled or batched? e.g., proxy emits aggregated receipt every 500ms with included nonce ranges and HMAC?

rachel: yes batching is primary. receipts replace per-request events for escrow flow; controller requests full audit fetch only on anomaly. we also attach a rotating escrow_id so controller can revoke mid-window.

emily: abuse detection: need heuristics beyond token counts. propose two signals: (1) behavioral anomalies (burst pattern divergence vs historical), (2) cost-signal (token_cost_per_req spike). require both before auto-revocation.

sec-bot: security note: escrow tokens must be bound to client cert CN or tenant API key to avoid token replay across tenants. also recommend rotating signing keys with a 1m grace cache on proxies.

vik: fairness: if many tenants hold escrowed capacity, proxies might still favour escrow over non-escrow requests. propose multi-queue admission: reserved queue for escrow (strict cap), best-effort queue for others, and a weighted deficit scheduler that enforces long-run fairness weights.

rachel: exactly. scheduler pseudocode sketch: 
```
if reserved_token.present: serve from reserved_queue
else: run weighted_deficit_round_robin(non_reserved_queues)
```
reserve leakage policy: unused reserved capacity decays back into best-effort pool after window_ms or explicit revoke.

emily: billing: escrowed capacity should be billed as a separate line-item (reservation fee + actual usage). also surface post-usage reconciliation to customers. need to ensure receipts are durable and tamper-evident. suggest append-only kafka topic "escrow.receipts.v1".

rachel: agreed. implementation checklist: token format, JWK signing endpoint, proxy validation + batched receipts, scheduler changes, billing pipeline hook, revoke API, telemetry.

vik: telemetry candidates: escrow_accept_rate, escrow_revoke_rate, escrow_unused_pct = sum(unused_reserved_tokens)/sum(granted_tokens), escrow_fraud_flag_rate. add per-tenant cost_skew_alert if tenant_token_cost / cohort_median > 3.

emily: rollout: 1) implement token validator + JWK endpoint, 2) proxies can accept tokens but only log decisions (no enforcement), 3) enable enforcement for internal tenants only, 4) expand to paid tenants. gated by fraud false-positive < 0.5% and escrow_unused_pct < 0.2.

sec-bot: ticket created: SEC-786 "escrow token security spec" assigned to @rachel

rachel: i'll write a short RFC addendum with the scheduler pseudocode and a small bench plan (multi-tenant with 10% escrowed). ping me with objections.

emily: :thumbsup:
